basic_info.description: My name is Vitaliy Vekslyer. I am an aspiring engineer enrolled in Engineering Physics @ SFU. I am always looking for new projects to work on and to gain experience from.

projects.title: Laser-writing Maskless Lithography Machine
projects.description: A laser-writing maskless lithography machine for 1μm feature size device microfabrication, built during a capstone design course at SFU, used as a modern alternative to the traditional photomask-based lithography machine in the SFU Engineering Science cleanroom. The machine uses a 405nm 1mW laser module to directly write patterns onto a photoresist-coated substrate, eliminating the need for photomasks and allowing rapid prototyping without the lengthy mask manufactuing process. The machine also allows use outside of the cleanroom, with its own air filtering mechanism. It comes with its own GUI with a controlled XYZ stage and camera, allowing for easier mark alignment.

projects.title: Stern-Gerlach Experiment Simulator
projects.description: A simple Stern-Gerlach experiment simulator made in C++ for PHYS 385 - Quantum II, Fall 2024. User can choose up to three SG machines and choose the initial state of the particles. Serves as an interactive visualization of the Stern-Gerlach experiment and the concept of quantum spin, to enhance understanding and modelling efforts of undergraduate students enrolled in quantum mechanics compared to other existing limited web-based simulators.

projects.title: Computer Vision-powered Visual Sepsis Detector
projects.description: Undergraduate research project of a computer-powered microscope for classification of sepsis-inducing bacteria using computer vision. I was the lead of the engineering team and had integrated a team of mechanical, electrical, computer and biomedical engineering students to create an actuator-powered automated microscope that moves around in an XY-axis to take pictures of a sample and then applies a deep learning model to classify different bacteria and assess a patient's risk of developing sepsis. This project is still ongoing as of July 2023, the device is ready but we require far more data for our model. I had worked closely with the CMOS image sensor, optics, and image processing of the device. Entire project was made in Simulink and MATLAB with use of Simscape to integrate together all mechanical, electrical and computer systems.

projects.title: Brain Computer Interface
projects.description:
I used OpenBCI's API and Machine Learning to control games made in Unity and PyGame.
 • Used OpenBCI API and neuromore to allow user to control a car game in Unity.
 • Implemented a machine learning inspired perceptron model to understand when user wishes to move the car forward.
 • Achieved 98% accuracy of user's intention to move the car.

projects.title: Asteroid Blaster
projects.description:
Asteroids clone made with C++ SDL. I wanted to know how games in C++ as well as GUIs are really being made and I came across SDL which I learnt a lot about while making this and a few other simple games.
 • Made using object-oriented principles.
 • Used knowledge of physics, algebra, trigonometry to implement simple 2D sprite movement.

projects.title: Exercise Journal
projects.description: The biggest collaborative project I had with seven other student developers. I delegated tasks using Agile PM principles and had worked closely with the frontend of the app with authentication of new users through the welcome screen.

projects.title: SFU OpFair 2024 Website
projects.description: Created the OpFair 2024 website; SFU's largest annual engineering, science and technology job fair hosted by the Faculty of Applied Sciences and the SFU Engineering Science Student Society. Allowed easier editing of website content for client through JSON. Used Python web scraping and Pillow to gather and process all images from previous OpFair website.

experience.title: Semiconductor Research Intern
highlights: Designed, fabricated, and evaluated AlN/AlGaN-based HEMTs to reduce power consumption and carbon footprint in power and RF electronics within NTT’s Multidisciplinary Materials Design and Science Laboratory (Thin-Film Materials Research Group).
Built optimization simulations using Silvaco TCAD, AMASS, and hand analysis via LaTeX; derived an optical phonon scattering model validated against Hall-effect measurements.

Performed characterization with Bruker AFM and composition/thickness analysis with Malvern Panalytical XRD; carried out device fabrication via photolithography and chemical/plasma etching (Nanosystems, SAMCO tools).
Evaluated device stacks and compositions to maximize drain current while minimizing gate leakage, supporting future AlN/AlGaN device research in the lab.

experience.title: Software Developer
highlights: Created full-stack applications in JavaScript/TypeScript, C#, React, Node.js and NestJS.
Worked on Sosido, a collaboration platform for medical research in Canada (https://www.sosido.com).
Developed a natural language statistical model enabling automated matching of Sosido’s users to recent publications, reducing missed user matches by as much as 75% and improving admin workflow.
Worked closely with clients, adapting to changing requirements and needs.
